{{nihongo|'''Aruka Shrine'''|有鹿神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Sagami Province]].

'''Aruka Shrine''' (Aruka-jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} whose main shrine is enshrined in {{ill|Kamigō|Q17226186|qid=Q17226186|lt=Kamigo}}, {{ill|Ebina, Kanagawa|Q734390|qid=Q734390}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|Q127513|qid=Q127513}}. The year of foundation is unknown, but a record notes that on November 19 of {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} 11 ({{ill|869|Q23917|qid=Q23917}}), its divine rank was promoted to Junior Fifth Rank Upper<ref>{{Cite book|Japanese |title=Rikkokushi Vol. 8 Sandai Jitsuroku, Vols. Upper & Lower |year=1930 |publisher=Asahi Shimbunsha |pages=407-408 |url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/1179599/1/225}}</ref>. It is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} compiled in {{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}} ({{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Engi}} 5) as one of the thirteen Shikinaisha shrines of {{ill|Sagami Province|Q1053732|qid=Q1053732}}, specifically the minor shrine Aruka Shrine (Arika no Kami no Yashiro) of Kōza District. By the late {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}}, it had become the {{ill|Chinjugami|Q97479976|qid=Q97479976|lt=general tutelary}} of five villages in Ebina-go<ref name=":3">{{Cite book|Japanese |title=Newly Edited Sagami Province Gazetteer |author=Mamiya Shisai |year=1875 |publisher=Cabinet Library |volume=65 |url=https://www.digital.archives.go.jp/item/4343246}}</ref>. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was designated a {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}, and today it is a Shinto religious corporation affiliated with {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|Q908077|qid=Q908077}}.

In recent years, the shrine has actively used {{ill|Social networking service|Q3220391|qid=Q3220391|lt=SNS}}, and its official character “{{ill|Aruka Shrine|Q11516854|qid=Q11516854|lt=Panda Chief Priest Proxy}}” has been featured in television media<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|date=2017-06-10|title=Broadcast List June 10: Ebina City|language=ja|website=Appare! KANAGAWA Daikōshin|publisher=TV Kanagawa|url=https://www.tvk-yokohama.com/appare/2017/06/610-2.php|access-date=2025-11-22}}</ref>.

=== Shrine Composition and Enshrinement Sites ===
Aruka Shrine is composed of three shrines—the Main Shrine (Hōmiya), Inner Shrine (Okunomiya), and Middle Shrine (Nakanomiya)—with its sphere of worship extending along the left bank of the middle reaches of the {{ill|Sagami River|Q612253|qid=Q612253}}, centered on the Katsusaka spring of the {{ill|Hato River|Q11675223|qid=Q11675223}} and the Ebina cultivated fields.

=== Main Shrine ===
Located in Kamigo, Ebina City, north of the Sagami River, the shrine stands on a well-drained {{ill|natural levee|Q11268410|qid=Q11268410}} formed by fluvial deposits at the confluence of the {{ill|Nakatsu River|Q11366442|qid=Q11366442|lt=Nakatsu River}}, {{ill|Koayu River|Q11464457|qid=Q11464457}}, and Hato River. The precinct faces Hachioji Road (Ebina City Road No. 17) to the south and southeast, while the {{ill|Yokosuka Waterway|Q11543536|qid=Q11543536|lt=Yokosuka Waterway}} partially divides the grounds on the east. Most of the area is designated as an Ebina City natural green conservation zone. The guardian forest known as Aruka no Mori<ref name=":0">“O-Aruka-sama and the Mizuhiki Festival Telling the History of Sagami-Nakahara,” Aruka Shrine Spiritual Culture Research Institute (2001)</ref> features zelkova as well as hackberry, tabunoki, ginkgo, and other trees, mainly on the northern side of the precinct. On the northwest side stands a south-facing wooden shrine building with copper roofing. The worship hall, offering hall, and protective hall form a three-in-one structure, with the main sanctuary covered by the protective hall. Other structures include torii gates, two pairs of guardian lion-dogs, two pairs of lanterns, two subsidiary shrines, a purification pavilion, bell tower, kagura hall doubling as a portable shrine hall, and a shrine office.

=== Inner Shrine ===
The Inner Shrine is enshrined in Aruka Valley at Katsusaka, Isobe, Minami Ward, {{ill|Sagamihara|Q209779|qid=Q209779}}. The valley lies west of {{ill|Katsusaka Site|Q11400214|qid=Q11400214}}, a nationally designated Jōmon-period archaeological site, beneath a {{ill|Fluvial terrace|Q1069618|qid=Q1069618|lt=fluvial terrace}} cliff. The surrounding {{ill|Laurel forest|Q788099|qid=Q788099}} is designated a natural monument of Sagamihara City<ref>{{Cite web|title=12. Katsusaka Evergreen Broadleaf Forest|url=https://www.city.sagamihara.kanagawa.jp/kankou/bunka/1022295/bunkazai/list/1010204/1010217.html|website=Sagamihara City|access-date=2025-11-23|language=ja}}</ref>. The site contains a stone torii, a stone shrine pedestal erected in {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 19 (1886) carved with boar, deer, and butterfly motifs, and a stone shrine built in {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 40 (1965). Following a small stream (Aruka Spring) northward leads to a spring emerging from the terrace cliff, known as Aruka Cave. This spring cave once had an opening about one shaku (approximately 30 cm) in diameter and served as the place where the sacred object was enshrined during the Mizuhiki Festival<ref>{{Cite book|Japanese |title=Kanagawa Prefecture Imperial Gazetteer Drafts, Vol. 2 |year=1964 |publisher=Kanagawa Prefectural Library |page=701 |url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/3022341/1/361}}</ref>, but it has since collapsed and been buried.

=== Middle Shrine ===
The Middle Shrine is located about 400 meters east-northeast of the Main Shrine in Kamigo, Ebina City. The precinct is small and surrounded by residential housing. At the entrance stands a stone monument reading “Aruka Pond,” a stone torii, and Aruka Pond (Aruka no Ike), associated with legends of discovering the sacred stone. The small, now-dry pond is crossed by a drum bridge, beyond which stands a stone shrine built in {{ill|1992|Q2060|qid=Q2060}} (Heisei 10). The land was donated to Aruka Shrine by its owner in November {{ill|938|Q24794|qid=Q24794}} (Shōwa 51)<ref>{{Cite book|Japanese |title=Exploring Ebina’s Historic Sites |year=1982 |publisher=Ebina City Agricultural Cooperative |url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/9538963}}</ref>. A legend remains that the sacred round stone flowed down from upstream of the Sagami River, was once worshipped at Katsusaka but declined, and eventually arrived at Aruka Pond<ref name=":2">{{Cite book|Japanese |title=Aruka Belief and Ichinomiya Traditions, Takachiho Ronso |author=Kojima Tsunekazu |year=2013 |publisher=Takachiho University Society |pages=1-24}}</ref>. A similar nearby legend in the {{ill|Suzuka-myojinsha|Q20045111|qid=Q20045111}} {{ill|Pratītyasamutpāda|Q522046|qid=Q522046}} recounts that when the Aruka deity and Suzuka deity fought, with aid from Suwa Myōjin and {{ill|Benzaiten|qid=Q818468|lt=Benzaiten}}, the Aruka deity was driven to Kamigo (see “{{ill|Suzuka-myojinsha|Q20045111|qid=Q20045111}}”<ref name=":1">Zama City History Source Series 1 “Zama Ancient Tales” (Zama City Library, March 31, 1987)</ref>).

=== Enshrined Deities and Sacred Objects ===
The current enshrined deities are two, together called '''Aruka Daimyōjin''', also known as O-Aruka-sama<ref name=":0" />.

* Aruka Hikono Mikoto  
* Aruka Hime no Mikoto  

Neither appears in the {{ill|Kiki (Shinto)|Q842308|qid=Q842308}}. Aruka Hikono Mikoto is a male solar deity worshipped at the Main and Middle Shrines, while Aruka Hime no Mikoto is a female water deity worshipped at the Inner and Middle Shrines<ref name=":0" />.

Additionally, the Kanagawa Prefectural Shrine Association website lists one deity, “Ōhirume no Muchi no Mikoto,” as enshrined<ref>{{Cite web|title=Aruka Shrine|url=https://www.kanagawa-jinja.or.jp/shrine/1207047-000/|website=Kanagawa Prefectural Shrine Association|access-date=2025-11-22|language=ja}}</ref>.

* {{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602|lt=Ōhirume no Muchi no Mikoto}}

This is considered an alternate name for Amaterasu Ōmikami, and “Ōhirume” appears as an enshrined deity of Aruka Shrine in the {{ill|Shinpen Sagami no Kuni Fudoki-kō|Q11503942|qid=Q11503942}}<ref name=":3" />; it is still worshipped at the Main Shrine today.

There are also various theories regarding past enshrined deities: “{{ill|Futodama|Q11059539|qid=Q11059539|lt=Futodama no Mikoto}}” in Nihon Sōkoku Fudoki and {{ill|Jinja Kakuroku|Q11590708|qid=Q11590708}}, “Ōhirume” (honji-butsu: Kokūzō) in the Newly Edited Sagami Province Gazetteer, “Aruka Hikono Mikoto” (honji-butsu: Dainichi Nyorai) in Takatakura Shaji-kō, “Adata Kashiwazu Hime” and “Aruka Ashitsu-me” in {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō Studies|Q11588824|qid=Q11588824}}, “Ōhirume no Muchi no Mikoto” and “Ukemochi no Kami” in Kōza District Shrine Summary, and in the “Aruka Shrine Worship Guide” produced during the tenure of former head priest Kojima Shigeharu, “Ōhirume no Muchi no Mikoto” with the accompanying “Aruka Hime.”

=== Sacred Objects ===
The sacred object of the Main Shrine is said to be a pale black round stone measuring five sun (about 15 cm) in height and nine sun (about 27 cm) in circumference<ref name=":3" />, enshrined in the inner sanctum. The sacred object of the Inner Shrine is considered to be the spring water emerging from Aruka Cave<ref name=":2" />.
